note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Books of Account to be Kept by Company
explain: Every company must prepare and keep books of account, relevant books and papers, and financial statements for every financial year.
Books must give a true and fair view of the state of affairs and be kept on an accrual basis using the double-entry system of accounting.
Records must be kept at the registered office. However, the Board may decide to keep them at any other place in India by filing Form AOC-5 with the Registrar within 7 days.

Electronic maintenance is permitted under Rule 3, provided books remain accessible in India, daily backups are saved on Indian servers, and software features an unalterable audit trail with edit logs (w.e.f. April 1, 2023).
Branch accounts kept in or outside India require quarterly summarized returns to be sent to the registered office.
Books of account and supporting vouchers must be preserved in good order for at least 8 years preceding the relevant financial year.

flow.title: Process of Maintaining and Preserving Books of Account
steps: Prepare books on accrual and double-entry basis
Keep records at registered office or notified place
Maintain mandatory audit trail if using accounting software
Receive quarterly branch summaries at registered office
Preserve books and vouchers for minimum 8 years

topics.example: XYZ Ltd keeps its physical accounting records at its corporate office in Mumbai instead of its registered office in Pune after passing a Board resolution and submitting Form AOC-5 to the ROC within 7 days.
remember: 8 years minimum preservation period for books and vouchers.
Form AOC-5 must be filed within 7 days if keeping books at another place in India.
Fine for default: ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 on managing director, CFO, or responsible person.
mistakes: Thinking that vouchers do not need to be preserved for 8 years along with books of account.
Believing companies can maintain books on a cash basis system of accounting.

quiz.q: Within how many days of a Board decision to keep books of account at a place other than the registered office must a company notify the ROC?
quiz.why: Section 128(1) proviso requires filing notice in Form AOC-5 with the Registrar within 7 days of the Board decision.

quiz.q: What is the minimum period for which books of account and vouchers must be preserved by a company?
quiz.why: Section 128(5) mandates preservation of books of account along with vouchers for at least 8 years immediately preceding the relevant financial year.

topics.title: Financial Statements
explain: Financial statements must give a true and fair view, comply with accounting standards notified under Section 133, and follow Schedule III format.
Insurance, banking, electricity supply, and specialized legal entities follow their respective governing Acts for specific disclosures instead of Schedule III.
Companies having one or more subsidiaries, associates, or joint ventures must prepare a Consolidated Financial Statement (CFS) and lay it before the AGM along with standalone statements.
Form AOC-1 contains the salient features of financial statements of subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures.

A intermediate subsidiary is exempt from preparing CFS if it is wholly owned (or partially owned without member objection), unlisted, and its ultimate/intermediate holding company files compliant CFS with the ROC.

flow.title: Financial Statement Compliance and Consolidation Flow
steps: Draft standalone financial statements per Schedule III
Ensure compliance with notified Accounting Standards
Prepare Consolidated Financial Statements if subsidiaries exist
Attach salient features of subsidiaries in Form AOC-1
Lay standalone and CFS before shareholders at AGM

topics.example: Alpha Ltd owns 100% of Beta Ltd. Alpha Ltd prepares its own standalone financial statements and also prepares consolidated statements combining Beta Ltd's figures to lay before its AGM.
remember: Form AOC-1 is used to present salient features of subsidiaries/associates/JVs.
Financial statements include Balance Sheet, P&L (or Income/Expenditure), Cash Flow Statement, Statement of Changes in Equity, and explanatory notes.
mistakes: Assuming small companies, One Person Companies (OPC), and dormant companies must compulsorily prepare a Cash Flow Statement.
Thinking non-compliance with Schedule III format is permissible if accounting standards are met.

quiz.q: Which form is used to attach the statement containing salient features of financial statements of subsidiaries/associates/JVs?
quiz.why: Rule 5 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 requires salient features of subsidiaries/associates/JVs to be reported in e-Form AOC-1.

quiz.q: Which of the following entities is exempt from mandatory inclusion of a Cash Flow Statement in its financial statements?
quiz.why: Section 2(40) exempts One Person Companies, small companies, dormant companies, and eligible private start-ups from preparing cash flow statements.

topics.title: Periodical Financial Results
explain: The Central Government may require prescribed classes of unlisted companies to prepare financial results on a periodical basis.
Companies covered under this provision must obtain approval of the Board of Directors for such periodical results.
The company must complete an audit or limited review of these periodical financial results as prescribed.
A copy of the periodical financial results must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the completion of the relevant period with prescribed fees.

flow.title: Steps for Periodical Financial Results
steps: Identify CG notification for unlisted company class
Prepare financial results for designated period
Obtain Board of Directors approval
Complete audit or limited review
File copy with ROC within 30 days

topics.example: An unlisted public company notified under Section 129A prepares half-yearly financial results, gets a limited review done by its auditor, and files the results with the ROC within 30 days.
remember: Section 129A applies to prescribed classes of unlisted companies.
Time limit for filing periodical financial results with ROC is 30 days.
mistakes: Confusing Section 129A periodical results with SEBI quarterly reporting rules for listed entities.

quiz.q: Within how many days of completion of the period must a company file its periodical financial results under Section 129A with the ROC?
quiz.why: Section 129A requires filing a copy of periodical financial results with the Registrar within 30 days of the end of the period.

quiz.q: What requirement must be completed before filing periodical financial results under Section 129A?
quiz.why: Section 129A mandates obtaining Board approval and completing an audit or limited review of the periodical results.

topics.title: Re-opening of Accounts on Court's or Tribunal's Orders
explain: A company cannot re-open its books of account or recast its financial statements voluntarily under Section 130; it requires an order from a Court or Tribunal.
An application for reopening can be made by CG, Income Tax authorities, SEBI, any statutory regulatory body, or any person concerned.
Grounds for order: Relevant earlier accounts were prepared in a fraudulent manner, OR affairs of the company were mismanaged casting doubt on accounting reliability.
Notice must be served to applicants/authorities, and their representations must be considered by the Court/Tribunal before passing an order.
Re-opening is permitted for a maximum of 8 financial years immediately preceding the current FY, unless CG issued a direction under Section 128(5) to preserve books for a longer period.
Accounts revised or re-casted under this section are final.

flow.title: Order of Re-opening Books of Account
steps: Application filed by CG, IT Dept, SEBI, or regulatory body
Court/Tribunal issues notice to applicants and concerned authorities
Court/Tribunal considers representations received
Order passed if fraud or severe mismanagement is proved
Books re-opened for up to 8 preceding FYs and finalized

topics.example: The Income Tax department discovers major fraud in accounts of FY 2019-20 during an assessment in FY 2024-25. IT Dept applies to NCLT under Section 130, and NCLT orders re-opening and recasting of accounts for FY 2019-20.
remember: Maximum limit for reopening: 8 financial years preceding current FY.
Order can only be made by a Court of competent jurisdiction or NCLT.
mistakes: Believing a company's Board of Directors can independently apply under Section 130 to reopen books of account.

quiz.q: What is the general maximum period for which books of account can be ordered to be re-opened under Section 130?
quiz.why: Section 130(3) restricts orders for re-opening books of account to a maximum of 8 financial years immediately preceding the current financial year.

quiz.q: Which of the following bodies CANNOT apply for re-opening of accounts under Section 130?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Individual Retail Customer with no legal standing
quiz.why: Section 130 specifies CG, IT authorities, SEBI, statutory regulatory bodies, or a person concerned as eligible applicants.

topics.title: Voluntary Revision of Financial Statements or Board's Report
explain: If directors find that financial statements (Sec 129) or Board's Report (Sec 134) do not comply with legal provisions, they may voluntarily prepare revised statements/reports.
Revision is allowed in respect of any of the 3 preceding financial years.
Requires prior approval of the Tribunal (NCLT) via application in Form No. NCLT-1 within 14 days of the Board decision.
The Tribunal gives notice to CG and Income Tax authorities and considers their representations before passing an order.
A certified copy of NCLT's order must be filed with the ROC within 30 days of receipt.
Revised statements/reports cannot be prepared or filed more than once in a financial year, and detailed reasons must be disclosed in the Board's report of the year of revision.

flow.title: Flow of Voluntary Revision under Section 131
steps: Board notes non-compliance in FS or Board Report
Apply to NCLT in Form NCLT-1 within 14 days
NCLT issues notice to CG and Income Tax authorities
NCLT approves revision; file order with ROC within 30 days
General meeting considers and adopts revised statements
File adopted revised statements with ROC within 30 days

topics.example: The Board of Directors of ABC Ltd realizes an error in statutory disclosures in the Board's report of FY 2022-23. They apply to NCLT under Section 131, receive approval, and revise the report after notifying ROC and members.
remember: Voluntary revision can cover any of the 3 preceding financial years.
Revision can be done only once in a single financial year.
mistakes: Confusing Section 130 (court-ordered re-opening due to fraud/mismanagement, up to 8 years) with Section 131 (voluntary Board revision due to non-compliance, up to 3 years).

quiz.q: Under Section 131, for how many preceding financial years can directors voluntarily revise financial statements or Board reports?
o: Any of the 3 preceding financial years
Any of the 5 preceding financial years
Any of the 8 preceding financial years
Only the immediate 1 preceding financial year
quiz.why: Section 131(1) permits voluntary revision in respect of any of the three preceding financial years.

quiz.q: Within how many days of receipt of NCLT's order approving voluntary revision must a certified copy be filed with the ROC?
quiz.why: Section 131(1) mandates filing the certified copy of NCLT order with the ROC within thirty days of receipt.

topics.title: National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
explain: NFRA is an independent regulatory authority constituted by CG (w.e.f. Oct 1, 2018) to oversee accounting and auditing standards and monitor auditor quality.

NFRA governs listed companies, unlisted public companies with paid-up capital ≥ ₹500 crore, turnover ≥ ₹1000 crore, or aggregate loans/debentures/deposits ≥ ₹500 crore, insurance/banking/power companies, and foreign entities based on thresholds.
Composition: A Chairperson (person of eminence) and up to 15 members (full-time and part-time).
Full-time members must not be associated with any audit firm during appointment and for 2 years after ceasing office.
NFRA has civil court powers under CPC 1908 (discovering documents, summoning persons, inspecting books).
Penalties for professional misconduct: Individual (₹1 lakh to 5 times fees received); Firm (₹5 lakh to 10 times fees received). Debarment from audit/valuation for 6 months to 10 years.

flow.title: NFRA Regulatory and Investigation Process
steps: Monitor compliance for governed companies and auditors
Initiate investigation suo moto or on CG reference
Exercise Civil Court powers to inspect and summon
Determine professional misconduct after hearing
Issue penalty order or debarment of auditor/firm
Appeals against order lie before Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT)

topics.example: NFRA investigates an audit firm auditing a listed pharma company for missing gross liability disclosures, proves professional misconduct, and imposes a penalty of ₹10 lakh while debarring the firm for 2 years.
remember: Full-time NFRA members cannot join audit firms during tenure and for 2 years post-tenure.
NFRA penalty: Min ₹1 lakh (individual) / ₹5 lakh (firm); max 5x fees (individual) / 10x fees (firm).
Debarment period: 6 months to 10 years.
mistakes: Believing ICAI or other bodies can parallelly continue misconduct proceedings once NFRA initiates investigation.

quiz.q: What is the maximum debarment period NFRA can impose on an auditor found guilty of professional misconduct?
quiz.why: Section 132(4)(c) empowers NFRA to debar a member or firm from undertaking audits/valuations for a period ranging from 6 months up to 10 years.

quiz.q: For how long after leaving office is a full-time NFRA member restricted from associating with any audit firm?
quiz.why: Section 132(3) mandates that full-time chairperson and members cannot be associated with audit firms during their appointment and for 2 years after.

topics.title: Central Government to Prescribe Accounting Standards
explain: Section 133 empowers the Central Government to prescribe accounting standards for companies in India.
Standards are prescribed based on recommendations made by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI).
The Central Government examines and consults with the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) before notifying standards.
Two sets of rules are notified under this section: Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021 and Companies (Indian Accounting Standards - Ind AS) Rules, 2015.

flow.title: Prescribing Accounting Standards Process
steps: ICAI formulates and recommends Accounting Standards
NFRA examines recommendations and advises CG
Central Government consults and reviews draft standards
CG notifies rules under Companies Act via MCA

topics.example: ICAI proposes amendments to revenue recognition guidelines. NFRA reviews them and recommends approval to MCA, which then notifies the updated Ind AS standard under Section 133.
remember: Accounting standards are recommended by ICAI and examined by NFRA before CG notification.
mistakes: Thinking ICAI can directly notify legally binding Accounting Standards without Central Government notification under Section 133.

quiz.q: Who has the authority to prescribe Accounting Standards for companies under Section 133?
quiz.why: Section 133 empowers the Central Government to prescribe accounting standards based on recommendations of ICAI in consultation with NFRA.

quiz.q: Which body formulates and initially recommends accounting standards to the Central Government?
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
quiz.why: Section 133 explicitly states standards are recommended by ICAI.

topics.title: Financial Statement, Board's Report, and Authentications
explain: Financial statements must be approved by the Board before signature and submission to auditors.
Signing requirement: Signed by Chairperson (if authorized by Board) OR by 2 directors (one being MD if any), AND by CEO, CFO, and CS (wherever appointed). OPC requires only 1 director.
Auditors' report and Board's report must be attached to every financial statement.
Board's Report content: Web link of annual return, Board meeting count, Directors' Responsibility Statement (DRS), fraud reports u/s 143(12), explanations on auditor qualifications, CSR details, etc.
Abridged Board Report (Rule 8A) applies to OPC and Small Companies.

Directors' Responsibility Statement (DRS) requires 6 specific board confirmations including compliance with AS, accounting policies, asset safeguarding, going concern, and internal financial controls (for listed co).
Penalty for default: Company ₹3,00,000; Every officer in default ₹50,000.

flow.title: Approval and Signing of Financial Statements and Board Report
steps: Board reviews and approves draft financial statements
Authorized directors (including MD), CEO, CFO, CS sign statements
Auditors issue Audit Report on signed statements
Board prepares and signs Board's Report (including DRS)
Audited FS, Audit Report, and Board Report circulated to members

topics.example: Vishwakarma Ltd has MD Mr. Indersen, director Mr. Hyder, and a Company Secretary. The FS must be signed by Mr. Indersen (MD), Mr. Hyder, and the CS before submitting to auditors.
remember: OPC financial statements need signature of only 1 director.
Penalty under Section 134: Company ₹3,00,000; Officer in default ₹50,000.
mistakes: Circulating unaudited financial statements to shareholders before AGM (invalid under Sec 134(7)).
Omitting signature of CS or CFO when such officers are appointed by the company.

quiz.q: Who among the following MUST sign the financial statements of a company if appointed, along with two directors?
quiz.why: Section 134(1) requires signatures of the Chairperson/2 directors (1 MD), plus CEO, CFO, and CS wherever appointed.

quiz.q: What is the penalty specified for an officer in default for non-compliance with Section 134?
quiz.why: Section 134(8) prescribes a penalty of ₹50,000 on every officer of the company who is in default.

topics.title: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
explain: CSR provisions apply to any company (including foreign branch/subsidiary) meeting any of these criteria in the immediately preceding FY: Net Worth ≥ ₹500 crore, Turnover ≥ ₹1000 crore, or Net Profit ≥ ₹5 crore (or having unspent CSR account balance).
CSR Committee requires 3 or more directors (at least 1 independent director). If CSR obligation ≤ ₹50 lakh, Board can discharge committee functions.
Mandatory spend: At least 2% of average net profits of preceding 3 financial years (or period since incorporation if < 3 years). Preference to local areas.
Administrative overheads capped at 5% of total CSR expenditure for the FY.
Unspent CSR funds (Ongoing projects): Transfer to 'Unspent CSR Account' within 30 days of FY end; spend within 3 FYs, else transfer to Schedule VII fund within 30 days of 3rd FY end.
Unspent CSR funds (Other than ongoing projects): Transfer to Schedule VII fund within 6 months of FY end.
Penalties for default: Company (twice unspent amount or ₹1 crore, whichever is less); Officer in default (1/10th unspent amount or ₹2 lakh, whichever is less).

flow.title: CSR Applicability and Spending Flow
steps: Check net worth/turnover/net profit thresholds for preceding FY
Constitute CSR Committee (or Board handles if spend ≤ ₹50 lakh)
Formulate CSR policy and annual action plan
Spend at least 2% of average net profit of 3 preceding FYs
Transfer unspent funds (30 days for ongoing / 6 months for others)
Report CSR details in Board's Report (Form CSR-2)

topics.example: MFL Ltd spent ₹40 lakh on CSR in FY 2024-25. Since its spend is below ₹50 lakh, it did not need to form a separate CSR Committee; its Board discharged all CSR functions directly.
remember: CSR Spend: 2% of average net profit of 3 immediately preceding FYs.
Ongoing project unspent transfer: 30 days to Unspent CSR Account.
Non-ongoing project unspent transfer: 6 months to Schedule VII Fund.
Administrative overhead limit: 5% of total CSR spend.
mistakes: Including employee welfare activities or political contributions as valid CSR spending.
Believing CSR applies only if all three criteria (Net worth, Turnover, Net profit) are satisfied together (satisfying any ONE is sufficient).

quiz.q: If a company's total CSR spending obligation for a financial year is ₹35 lakh, is it required to constitute a CSR Committee?
o: Yes, mandatory for all covered companies
No, Board of Directors can discharge CSR functions if spend does not exceed ₹50 lakh
Yes, if it is a listed company only
quiz.why: Section 135(9) states that if the amount to be spent does not exceed ₹50 lakh, CSR Committee constitution is not mandatory and Board discharges functions.

quiz.q: Within how many months of FY expiry must unspent CSR funds for a non-ongoing project be transferred to a Schedule VII Fund?
quiz.why: Section 135(5) second proviso requires unspent amounts for non-ongoing projects to be transferred to a Schedule VII fund within 6 months of the expiry of the financial year.

topics.title: Right of Members to Copies of Audited Financial Statement
explain: Every member, debenture trustee, and entitled person has a right to receive copies of audited financial statements (including CFS), auditor's report, and Board's report.
Document circulation timeline: At least 21 days before the AGM (14 days for Section 8 companies).
Shorter notice circulation is valid if agreed by members holding at least 95% of paid-up share capital giving voting rights (or 95% total voting power if no share capital).
Mode of delivery: Electronic mode for listed/public companies (Net Worth > ₹1 cr & Turnover > ₹10 cr) for demat shareholding with registered email; physical dispatch for others.
Listed companies can send salient features summary in Form AOC-3 / AOC-3A provided full statements are kept open for inspection at registered office 21 days prior to AGM.
Listed companies must host standalone and subsidiary financial statements on their website.
Penalty for default: Company ₹25,000; Officer in default ₹5,000.

flow.title: Circulation of Financial Statements Flow
steps: Prepare audited FS, CFS, Auditor's Report, and Board Report
Send copies electronically or physically to members and trustees
Ensure dispatch at least 21 days prior to AGM (14 days for Sec 8)
Host statements on company website (for listed companies)
Keep records open for inspection at registered office

topics.example: Listed company RELM Ltd hosts its audited standalone and consolidated financial statements on its website 21 days before AGM, and dispatches electronic summaries in AOC-3 to demat shareholders.
remember: Circulation limit: Minimum 21 days before AGM (14 days for Section 8 Co).
Shorter notice consent threshold: 95% of voting paid-up share capital or total voting power.
Penalty: Company ₹25,000; Officer in default ₹5,000.
mistakes: Assuming listed companies can skip hosting foreign subsidiary accounts on their website if foreign law doesn't require audit (unaudited statements must still be posted).

quiz.q: What is the minimum statutory notice period for circulating financial statements before an AGM for a Section 8 company?
quiz.why: Via Notification GSR 466(E), Section 8 companies require a notice period of 14 days instead of 21 days.

quiz.q: What is the penalty imposed on a company for failing to comply with Section 136 provisions?
quiz.why: Section 136(3) specifies a company penalty of ₹25,000 for non-compliance.

topics.title: Filing Copy of Financial Statement with Registrar
explain: A copy of financial statements (including CFS) adopted at AGM, with all attached documents, must be filed with the ROC within 30 days of AGM (OPC within 180 days of FY end).
Filing forms: Form AOC-4 (Standalone), Form AOC-4 CFS (Consolidated), Form AOC-4 NBFC (for Ind AS NBFCs), and Form CSR-2 (CSR report).
Mandatory XBRL filing (Form AOC-4 XBRL): Listed co & Indian subsidiaries, companies with paid-up capital ≥ ₹5 crore, turnover ≥ ₹100 crore, or all Ind AS compliant companies.
If AGM is not held: File FS + statement of facts and reasons for not holding AGM within 30 days of the last date on which AGM should have been held.
If FS is not adopted at AGM: File un-adopted FS within 30 days as provisional; file adopted FS within 30 days of adjourned AGM.
Penalty for default: Company (₹10,000 + ₹100/day, max ₹2,00,000); MD/CFO/Director in default (₹10,000 + ₹100/day, max ₹50,000).

flow.title: Filing Financial Statements with ROC
steps: Financial statements adopted at AGM
Prepare Form AOC-4 / AOC-4 CFS / AOC-4 XBRL and Form CSR-2
File with ROC within 30 days of AGM (180 days of FY end for OPC)
If un-adopted, file provisional copy within 30 days of AGM
File final adopted statements within 30 days of adjourned AGM

topics.example: Sun Ltd holds its AGM on Aug 31, but adjourns without adopting accounts pending CAG comments. Sun Ltd must file un-adopted accounts as provisional with ROC within 30 days of Aug 31, and file adopted accounts within 30 days of the adjourned AGM.
remember: 30 days from AGM date to file AOC-4 with ROC (180 days from FY end for OPC).
XBRL filing criteria: Listed co, Paid-up capital ≥ ₹5 cr, Turnover ≥ ₹100 cr, or Ind AS applicability.
Once XBRL reporting starts, company must continue XBRL filing in future years regardless of criteria.
mistakes: Failing to file provisional financial statements with ROC when AGM adjourns without adopting accounts.
Assuming OPCs must file financial statements within 30 days of AGM (OPCs do not hold AGMs and get 180 days from FY closure).

quiz.q: Within how many days from the closure of the financial year must a One Person Company (OPC) file its adopted financial statements with the ROC?
quiz.why: Section 137(1) mandates an OPC to file its financial statements within 180 days from the closure of the financial year.

quiz.q: Which of the following companies is mandatorily required to file financial statements in XBRL format under Rule 3(1)?
o: Private company with paid-up capital of ₹2 crore
Unlisted company with turnover of ₹120 crore
Small company with turnover of ₹10 crore
Section 8 company with turnover of ₹25 crore
quiz.why: Rule 3(1) of Companies (Filing in XBRL) Rules requires companies with turnover of ₹100 crore or above to file in e-form AOC-4 XBRL.

topics.title: Internal Audit
explain: Section 138 read with Rule 13 mandates internal audit for specified classes of companies.
Mandatory for: All Listed Companies.

Mandatory for Unlisted Public Companies meeting ANY of these in preceding FY: Paid-up share capital ≥ ₹50 crore, Turnover ≥ ₹200 crore, Outstanding loans/borrowings from banks/PFIs > ₹100 crore (at any point), or Outstanding deposits ≥ ₹25 crore (at any point).
Mandatory for Private Companies meeting ANY of these in preceding FY: Turnover ≥ ₹200 crore, or Outstanding loans/borrowings from banks/PFIs > ₹100 crore (at any point).
Who can be internal auditor: Chartered Accountant, Cost Accountant, or any other professional decided by the Board.
Internal auditor may or may not be an employee of the company, and CA/CMA need not be in practice.
Audit Committee or Board, in consultation with Internal Auditor, formulates scope, functioning, periodicity, and methodology.

flow.title: Internal Audit Applicability and Appointment Flow
steps: Check company class (Listed / Unlisted Public / Private)
Evaluate preceding FY thresholds (Capital, Turnover, Loans, Deposits)
Board appoints CA, Cost Accountant, or designated professional
Audit Committee/Board formulates scope and periodicity
Internal auditor conducts audit and submits reports to Board

topics.example: SDF Ltd, an unlisted public company, had an outstanding bank loan of ₹100.59 crore on Sept 30, 2025. Because borrowings crossed ₹100 crore at a point in the preceding FY, it must mandatorily appoint an internal auditor.
remember: Unlisted Public Co thresholds: Capital ≥ ₹50cr, Turnover ≥ ₹200cr, Loans > ₹100cr, Deposits ≥ ₹25cr.
Private Co thresholds: Turnover ≥ ₹200cr, Loans > ₹100cr.
Internal Auditor can be an employee or external professional, and CA/CMA need not hold certificate of practice.
mistakes: Believing private companies are tested for deposit thresholds or paid-up capital thresholds for internal audit (only turnover and loans apply to private co).
Assuming internal auditor must mandatory be a Chartered Accountant in practice.

quiz.q: Which threshold triggers mandatory internal audit for a Private Company under Rule 13 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014?
o: Paid-up share capital of ₹50 crore or more
Outstanding deposits of ₹25 crore or more
Turnover of ₹200 crore or more during preceding FY
Net profit of ₹5 crore or more
quiz.why: Rule 13(1)(c) specifies turnover of ₹200 crore or more (or bank loans exceeding ₹100 crore) for private companies.

quiz.q: Can an employee of a company be appointed as its Internal Auditor under Section 138?
o: No, internal auditor must be an independent practicing firm
Yes, internal auditor may or may not be an employee of the company
Yes, but only if approved by NCLT
No, strictly prohibited by Companies Act
quiz.why: Explanation to Rule 13(1) states that internal auditor may or may not be an employee of the company.
